classification.difficultyReason: Infer that the surrounding path adds twice its width to each pool dimension, model the total area, solve for a positive width and convert metres to centimetres before rounding.

content.prompt:
A pool measuring 6 m by 3 m is to have a path surrounding it.
If the total area of the pool and path is to be $31\text{ m}^2$, find the width ($x$ m) of the path, correct to the nearest cm.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 6, nested rectangles below the prompt
spec.description: Two unshaded rectangles with a uniform gap. The inner rectangle represents the pool and carries the 6 m and 3 m labels. A horizontal double-headed arrow spans the right-hand gap and is labelled x m.
spec.mathematics: The pool is 6 m by 3 m. A path of uniform width x surrounds it, giving outer dimensions 6+2x and 3+2x metres. Drawing coordinates are schematic and supply no additional measurements.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; no solution values are shown.

answer.short: $63\text{ cm}$. Use $(6+2x)(3+2x)=31$ and take the positive root.
answer.worked:
The outer rectangle measures $(6+2x)$ m by $(3+2x)$ m.
$$\begin{align*}
(6+2x)(3+2x)&=31\\
4x^2+18x+18&=31\\
4x^2+18x-13&=0
\end{align*}$$
With $a=4$, $b=18$ and $c=-13$,
$$\begin{align*}
x&=\frac{-18\pm\sqrt{18^2-4(4)(-13)}}{2(4)}\\
x&=\frac{-18\pm\sqrt{532}}{8}\\
x&=\frac{-9\pm\sqrt{133}}{4}.
\end{align*}$$
Reject the negative root because the path width must be positive.
$$\begin{align*}
x&=\frac{-9+\sqrt{133}}{4}\text{ m}\\
x&\approx 0.63314\text{ m}.
\end{align*}$$
The width is approximately $63.314$ cm, so it is $\boxed{63\text{ cm}}$ to the nearest centimetre.
